title: Research roundup: 6 cool science stories we almost missed
gist: September's science roundup covers a tentative LUX-ZEPLIN dark matter hint, ATLAS observing entangled Z bosons at the highest energy yet, a yeast-and-gelatin Martian building material, 25,000-year-old betel nut use, a possible Galileo four-lens telescope from 1630, and 1830s cosmoramas used as property marketing.

insights.claim: The LUX-ZEPLIN detector in a South Dakota gold mine may have recorded a possible WIMP dark matter event, presented at a 2026 conference and submitted to Physical Review Letters, but it is well below the confirmation threshold and could be a statistical fluke.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A long-running null search is producing an unexplained event; follow-up data from XENONnT and PandaX will test it, but past anomalies have faded.
insights.quote: the signal is just a hint, well below the threshold needed to confirm discovery, and might just be a statistical fluke
insights.locator: The announcement came with strong caveats

insights.claim: The event had higher nuclear recoil energy than expected for a standard WIMP, yet the detector did not also record the lower-energy WIMPs that should accompany it, pushing theorists toward models in which interaction rate rises with energy or WIMPs have internal structure.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: If real, the signal would break standard WIMP models and redirect direct-detection experiments.
insights.locator: If it turns out to be a WIMP that struck

insights.claim: LUX-ZEPLIN and XENONnT at Gran Sasso are still collecting data and China's PandaX detector is under construction, so independent confirmation or refutation should come from competing xenon experiments.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Watch for XENONnT results as the near-term test of the anomaly.

insights.claim: ATLAS physicists observed entanglement in pairs of Z bosons, which the authors claim is the highest-energy example of entanglement observed to date, following a 2023 observation in top-quark pairs.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Colliders are becoming a testbed for quantum foundations, relevant to long-run quantum technology science.
insights.quote: highest-energy example of entanglement observed to date
insights.locator: Z bosons are produced when a Higgs boson decays

insights.claim: Entanglement is described as the foundation for quantum computing and next-generation sensors, though it is normally delicate and decoheres quickly under interference.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Decoherence is the key engineering constraint for quantum computing and sensing businesses.
insights.locator: Maintaining quantum entanglement is usually a delicate process

insights.claim: Hong Kong engineers made a building material from Martian rock simulant, gelatin and a protein-coated yeast that freeze-dries on exiting a 3D-printer nozzle into a porous foam with 10 to 12 MPa compressive strength, comparable to cheap concrete.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
entities: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
insights.so_what: A cheap in-situ resource approach attacks the main cost of off-world habitat, transport mass, though it is lab-scale.
insights.locator: They found that the mixture freeze-dries

insights.claim: The process is less energy-intensive than melting Martian rock into bricks and the yeast can be recycled from dismantled structures, while Mars gravity at about a third of Earth's means structures could be much taller than Earth-equivalent one- or two-story builds.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Energy and recyclability advantages would matter for any future Mars or lunar construction economics.
insights.locator: Per the authors, that is strong enough

themes.theme: Betel nut use in the Late Pleistocene

insights.claim: Griffith University archaeologists found tooth grooves on two Sulawesi forager skeletons, one dated 25,000 to 16,000 years ago, consistent with sucking betel nuts and suggesting psychoactive plant use as early as the Late Pleistocene.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Pushes back the known date of habitual psychoactive use, relevant to the long history of stimulant markets.
insights.locator: Now Griffith University archaeologists have discovered

insights.claim: Authors posit betel nut sucking began as toothache relief since arecoline is a natural analgesic, but abrasive seeds wore teeth down to the pulp chambers, creating a cycle of habitual use and worse dental health.
insights.speaker: Adam Brumm, co-author
insights.so_what: An early example of a remedy that creates its own dependency loop.
insights.quote: years of prolonged nut-sucking eventually caused much worse dental health problems, creating a cycle of continued habitual use
insights.locator: The authors posit that people from that period

themes.theme: History of technology: Galileo's telescope and cosmoramas

insights.claim: A University of Limerick historian found a 1666 manuscript by Friar Ignacio Muñoz describing a four-lens telescope attributed to Galileo, which if correct would push the four-lens design back to 1630 at the latest versus the first known examples around 1643.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Revises the timeline of optical innovation, an example of overlooked archives rewriting technology provenance.
insights.locator: Galileo swore never to sell any of his telescopes

insights.claim: In the 1830s, London auctioneer Brooks and Hedger used cosmoramas to market estates, an early form of virtual property tours, though costly enough to be reserved for luxury properties and abandoned by 1860.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Immersive property marketing has a long history, and it only survived once production costs fell, as with modern virtual tours.
insights.locator: John Plunkett, a historian at the University of Exeter
